author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Republicans claim to be the party that cuts the job-killing capital gains tax, not raises it. However, due to a quirk in the Senate-passed tax bill, the tax on capital gains might go up — and for some types of long-held assets, it could rise substantially.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: It seems the Southern Poverty Law Center, a supposed champion of civil rights, might have secretly funded white supremacist groups. According to a superseding indictment by the Department of Justice, the SPLC allegedly paid informants to promote and fund racist groups while publicly denouncing them. The organization also created fake entities to conceal its funding from donors.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — No, friends, Romans, countrymen, it wasn't enough to destroy the White House Rose Garden. It wasn't enough to tear down the stately East Wing, where guests once mingled. It wasn't enough to replace "John F. Kennedy" with "Donald J. Trump" on the national performing arts center's marble wall.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: You may wonder why President Donald Trump is doing everything he can, day by day, to destroy faith in democracy in little and large ways, on the job day and night. I have an answer that will presently be revealed.

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: Socialism always finds an audience, appealing to base envy and resentment. Labeling "oligarchs," "Wall Street barons," "kulaks," or "billionaires" as scapegoats is easy and cheap. It was refreshing to hear Jeff Bezos, the fourth richest man, praise capitalism's moral and economic superiority in his recent interview with Andrew Ross Sorkin on CNBC.

author: connie-schultz
label: Left-wing
text: Many of us are feeling a lot of excitement, bolstered by wave after wave of relief. We are a nation of survivors. On Inauguration Day, I felt hopeful watching Joe Biden and Kamala Harris take their oaths of office. They appeared to understand what we were asking of them and accepted without reservation.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — Something told me to get to East Potomac Park before Donald Trump could destroy it. Sure enough, I did on a rainy Sunday morning for a rally to protect the waterfront parkland from his axe. The next weekend, he cut down 430 trees — for a fancy golf course, of course. He sneakily started on a Saturday morning during the three-day holiday weekend.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Folks, our country is on a slippery slope. We need to stop it before it's too late. We haven't even hit Thanksgiving, and already the war on Christmas is in full swing. One of the largest public school systems in the U.S. is now eliminating every reference to religious holidays from its official calendar.

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text: "We didn't mark the Fourth of July," he told me. "For us, it was the day Vicksburg fell." Vicksburg, Mississippi, fell to Union troops on July 4, 1863. The Confederates surrendered, as was their habit. Long memories still mourn the Lost Cause of Black backs whipped bloody.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: As the House and Senate work through the tax cut and reform effort, let me make one thing clear: Both plans are pro-growth, with the economic power coming from the business side. But where it comes from the personal side, there will be very little growth. That was always the bet.

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: The U.S. national debt now exceeds $40 trillion, doubling in less than a decade. Politicians on both sides have reacted with typical fiscal games: finger-pointing. Democrats blame Republican tax cuts, while Republicans blame Democratic spending. But both parties are culpable, each hiding behind a lie of omission. And if we let them, they'll keep us crashing into the same fiscal wall together.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: We said on 9/11 that we'd "never forget." But with our president's no-strategy approach to combating Islamic extremists, doesn't Washington seem to be ignoring its commitment to our remembrance, as well as its duty to safeguard our land and liberties?

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text: Way back there in the 1700s and the 1800s, the British conquered a big chunk of the world thanks to their navy, which was crewed by whip-scarred, toothless, unwilling sailors with untreated syphilis. That's who you want to fight your wars. No one fights like mistreated men living on a diet of garbage, the lash, and below-decks rape.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: After 5 1/2 bumpy years of controversial service, the besieged but bolstered attorney general, Eric Holder, resigned. But is Eric Holder really stepping down for some benign reason at a critical time for our country, or is there a sinister and strategic plan behind it all?

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text: I was working at a medium-sized city newspaper on Sept. 11, 2001. No one had stormed the Capitol yet, there hadn't been any George Floyd riots, we hadn't started the war we were going to lose in Afghanistan, and ICE hadn't killed anyone in the street.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Greg Abbott, the right-wing hack who is governor of Texas, probably doesn't know what a "petard" is, but he's now been hoist on a petard. "Hoist on a petard" is a Shakespearean phrase for a bomb maker being blown sky-high by his own creation.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Financial markets and most media pundits are overlooking the new trends. With shrewd moves by President Trump, the likelihood of significant tax cuts in the next 10 weeks has sharply increased.

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: French economist Gabriel Zucman has returned to California with a familiar French solution to a fiscal issue: another tax. Based at UC Berkeley, Zucman now supports Proposition 40, which would impose a 5% tax on Californians with net worth over $1 billion. Zucman, coauthor of the proposition, estimates that this tax could raise about $100 billion, with 90% of the proceeds earmarked for healthcare.

author: chuck-norris
label: Right-wing
text: Last week, when "Fox & Friends" discussed my latest column, "Neutering Religious Holidays," liberals sprang into action to defend President Barack Obama's record. So I decided to investigate and see how spiritually his Thanksgiving addresses have been in the past and compare them with those of our founding president, George Washington.

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: "The rich are different from you and me." — F. Scott Fitzgerald. I read two books in one weekend: "Just Mercy" by Bryan Stevenson on Saturday, "Strangers" by Belle Burden on Sunday. They're true stories, told well, about two countries, both inside America's borders: Death Row in Alabama, Martha's Vineyard in Massachusetts.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: From Q-Anon nuttiness to JD Vance's "Deep State" quackery, wacko right-wing conspiracies have infiltrated the center of Republican politics. But don't let their goofiness obscure the fact that there is indeed a very real plot to rig America's economic and political system, causing wealth and power to flow uphill — from the workaday majority to moneyed elites.

author: connie-schultz
label: Left-wing
text: After I began writing a column in the fall of 2002, it wasn't long before I received regular letters from those who used God as a cudgel against LGBTQ rights. This was unsurprising. At the time, I was on staff at The Plain Dealer in Cleveland, and I was well acquainted with the bigotry in my home state. Most of the hate mail came from strangers, but I also got lectures from family members. Few things infuriate right-wing Christians more than a relative insisting they know a different God.

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: There's an old saying: Those who can, do; those who can't, teach. A similar idea underlies the discussion about wealth taxes in California and elsewhere: Those who can, build companies. Those who can't, find ways for the government to take shares in what others have built.

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing
text: Classic Labor Day imagery shows men in hard hats and tough women in uniforms. These are Americans who did not build their muscles at a wellness club. In contrast, actual photos of the Democratic Socialists of America show seas of white faces belonging to college graduates. The only work most of them have done with their hands is typing. But the DSA is run by leaders who pretend otherwise, pushing forward candidates who play-act as tradespeople.

author: froma-harrop
label: Left-wing
text: Oh good, another war. This time a trade war with Canada and for no other reason than ... what? To give Donald Trump a new stage for big-league bullying? To divert attention from the Jeffrey Epstein files? Who knows. Whatever. Trying to humiliate our closest ally does not serve American interests, does it?

author: david-harsanyi
label: Right-wing
text: The next mayor of Washington, D.C. is likely to be a Marxist, as Los Angeles sees a battle between Mensheviks and Bolsheviks for control, and New York City has already succumbed to a champion of Third Worldism.

author: marc-dion
label: Left-wing
text:

Good examples are Donald Trump, escargot, and gang rape, three things that disgust me but are desired by some. Knowing this will make you hesitate before sitting next to a stranger on the bus. The fact that I can type "bus" without thinking of "school" suggests I might have some acquaintance with people whose wants and needs are not only disgusting but poorly concealed.

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing
text: Brides should be aware they already have a man; they don't need their wedding to find a date for Saturday night. They've supposedly secured one for the future. So, it's puzzling how the "naked dressing" trend, deplorable even at clubs, has infiltrated wedding customs. This started as a fashion move by celebrities seeking attention, now it's happening on the aisle.

author: lawrence-kudlow
label: Right-wing
text: Last week, Donald Trump scaled back his initial call for a punitive and blanket tariff on steel and aluminum. Good move. The financial markets responded positively, as the revised plan focuses on countries that are cheating and stealing, notably China and Russia, while offering exemptions to allies.

author: froma-harrop
label: Left-wing
text: About three weeks before Republicans expected an electoral setback, Donald Trump had to remove Kimberly Guilfoyle, his ambassador to Greece. He simply had to. Trump's money-grubbing corruption was becoming tiresome even to his loyal supporters, but the president knew how to cloak his mob-like patter in foggy euphemisms and double meanings.
